title: Canonical proper-support maps into compact cohomology
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative coefficient ring of the small-site size, $f:X\to B$ a scheme morphism with a proper compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\to B)$, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with $Z\to B$ proper. Use [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] for $C_i\dashv R\Gamma_Z$, and [def-pur-compact-product-arrows] for $R\Gamma_c^c$. The composite $\bar i=i j$ is closed. The ordinary restriction isomorphism $j^*C_{\bar i}\cong C_i$ is uniquely normalized by its equality on the quotient from the constant sheaf; derive this isomorphism and define $j_!C_i\to C_{\bar i}$ as the open-adjunction mate of its inverse. This map is invertible because the support is contained in the open. Define the constant-section unit $M\to R\Gamma(\bar X,C_{\bar i}M)$ as the support-adjunction unit followed by forgetting support. For $\alpha:C_iM\to K$, define its compact image by this unit, the inverse coefficient-extension map, and $R\Gamma(j_!\alpha)$. Define $u_Z$ by taking $M=R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$ and $\alpha$ the support counit. Define restriction of support complexes as the transpose of the restricted support counit under the normalized coefficient restriction. For any extension $F$ and specified $e:j^*F\cong K$, define excision as this restriction followed by $R\Gamma_Z(e)$, and define $R\Gamma_c^c K\to R\Gamma(\bar X,F)$ by the open-adjunction mate of $e^{-1}$. The product support of two proper supports is proper. The Leray composition isomorphism identifies these compact sections with $R\Gamma(B,Rf_!^c(-))$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. For finite A, use the closed-support adjunction of [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product] to make the same normalized coefficient, constant-unit, counit, class-image, excision and extension constructions on the small pro-etale sites when both ambient schemes are locally Noetherian. For finite-type schemes over a field and their proper compactifications, obtain those Noetherian structures from the structure maps, without adding hypotheses. The pro-etale class-morphism type and its support-adjunction transpose are retained for arbitrary coefficient complexes and shifts.
